questions.stem: What makes a drug usable as an induction agent?
Which four IV agents are the usual induction agents?
Why are benzodiazepines and opioids not usually used alone to induce anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Onset is unpredictable and action is long at induction doses

questions.stem: Apart from IV agents, what other induction approach is described?
questions.answer: Inhalational, or a combination of both

questions.stem: Which induction agent belongs to the phenol chemical class?
Which induction agent is a barbiturate?
Which induction agent is an imidazole?
Which induction agent belongs to the phencyclidine class?
Which induction agent is a benzodiazepine?
What happens to an IV induction agent once it is in the plasma?
questions.answer: Part binds plasma protein; the rest is free

questions.stem: In order, what circulatory route does an IV induction bolus take to reach the brain?
questions.answer: Venous blood, right heart, lungs, left heart, systemic circulation

questions.stem: What share of cardiac output goes to the vessel-rich organs (brain, liver, kidney)?
Which form of an induction agent crosses the blood-brain barrier fastest?
What is known about how IV induction agents act at receptor level?
questions.answer: Exact mechanism unknown; GABA-A, NMDA and acetylcholine receptors are candidate sites

questions.stem: Why does more induction agent reach the brain in shock and the elderly?
questions.answer: A larger share of cardiac output goes to the brain

questions.stem: How does low cardiac output affect the onset of an IV induction agent?
options: Speeds onset because the drug is cleared faster
Delays onset by slowing arrival at the brain
No effect on onset at all
Shortens the action of the agent

questions.stem: In induction for low cardiac output states, what is the key to safety?
questions.answer: Slow titration of a reduced dose
